# Finite ADT first studies

The inert [archive](first.tar.xz) and [index](index.json) preserve all sixty
original files from two informed pre-implementation studies at `0bd10818`.
Complete first sources, predictions, raw observations, observers as data and
monitored before/after maps remain unchanged. Readers never extract or run them.

The source study has ten complete projects and twelve CLI observations: four
successful existing Bit/qif controls and eight refusals. Seven desired
enum/record/match/qmatch forms stop in parsing; those failures do not validate
later type, effect, ownership or coherent-control rules. The direct ordinary
if on Q<Bit> reaches a type refusal. Controls use at most two qubits. These are
observations of the selected prior binaries, not a clean-build attestation.

The separate Lean study uses logical dimension three and physical dimension
four. Its first elaboration fails because `Except` lacks an inferred equality
instance. Printed `sorryAx` placeholders belong to that failed elaboration;
they are not accepted proofs. A separate version derives structural equality
and corrects the observer's overstrong expectation of axiom-free output.
All fifteen concrete theorems then elaborate using only `propext`, against
the observed compiled Lean 4.30.0 imports. No project axiom, `native_decide`,
runtime override, unsafe or partial definition is introduced.

The facts distinguish logical cardinality from physical width, preserve full
relative phase, reject wrong dependency/axis equations and separate a code's
left inverse from a whole-space isometry. The current Encoding reader's
Bits<2> refusal remains unchanged. Monitored source/native/study/import bytes
are stable inside both windows; this is not a fresh replay of the imports.

The archive contains 30,807,429 original file bytes in 862,696 compressed bytes.
Its bounded passive checks preserve both attempts and their different scopes.
No ADT/qmatch implementation, generic/reference-safe or source-preservation
theorem, independent human specification review, accepted handle, guarantee or
Issue completion follows from this history. Current implementation and fresh
validation are separate work under #64/#195; #39/#63 remain excluded.
